answer: In a market where agents earn reputation through completed jobs, each new identity starts with no history and must post a bond before accepting valuable work. A verifier releases payment only after checking the result, and fraud burns the bond while adding a public penalty tied to the account’s funding source. The vine of trusted referrals can grow across a trellis of audited transactions, but an island of freshly minted accounts cannot borrow that history. A sybil attacker must therefore lock up real capital per identity and risk losing it repeatedly.
